server.name: parallax-coordinator
server.title: Parallax
server.description: Parallax Desktop's coordinator: start, steer, read and land the coding-agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, jcode, cloud machines) running on a person's machine, and talk to the other agents it runs.

protocolMetadata.instructions: You reach the coding agents of one person through their Parallax Desktop. list_sessions shows every agent you may message: their Codex, Claude Code, jcode and Parallax sessions and the project's other Capy threads. Pass as (your own Capy thread id, which thread_get "this" reads) on every call, so your messages come from your thread and answers come back to it. send_to messages one, and it arrives in that agent's terminal (or thread) as one line starting [a2a <id> from <you>]. Messages to you arrive in your thread as [a2a <id> from …] <text>; answer them with reply, that message id and the same as. Replies arrive the same way, so end your turn instead of polling; inbox reads them too, and inbox with wait blocks until one arrives when you cannot go on without it. Send only a task, new information, a result or a blocker; skip routine progress and acknowledgement-only replies. Prefer 1–3 sentences: outcome or question first, essential constraints and evidence next, with references (paths, commits, PRs, session ids) instead of pasted logs or plans. Keep necessary detail; never send secrets. Delegate the outcome and let the recipient plan the work. Reply in the existing thread, and request a reply only when needed. When a [Parallax review] message arrives, review_findings reads every finding of it, not only those the message shows. To see or work the person's Parallax window, use window_read (its controls as rows), window_act (press, focus or set one by id, in the background) and window_shot (a picture rendered offscreen). Never drive the person's screen, mouse or keyboard (computer use, a browser, screenshots of their display), and never ask another agent to. Never end a turn asking leave for a step your standing rules already authorize (verify, continue, proceed, fix a finding, rerun or retry, merge once the covering tests pass outside held paths): do it, then report what you did. Ask the person only for what they alone decide: a held path, money, credentials, deploys,

tool.description: Send a short message to one of the sessions list_sessions shows (by id, an id prefix of 4 or more, or its title as a slug), a local agent, a Codex or Claude Code session, or another Capy thread. mode steer (the default) types it into the agent now and a busy agent takes it at its next step; queue holds it until the agent goes quiet; interrupt stops its current generation first. tool.name: log_error
tool.title: File an error in Parallax's logs
tool.description: File a failure in Parallax's logs database with its evidence, so it can be fixed from what you saw: Parallax misbehaving (a tool that hung or failed, a wrong answer, the app slow) or anything you want a fixer to have. Give a one-line title, what happened in body, the log lines or output you saw in logs, and files (paths in your worktree: a trace, a screenshot) as evidence. Parallax adds its own log lines from that moment and a system snapshot, redacts secrets from all of it, and answers the entry's id and the command a fixer pulls it with. Repeats of the same title fold into one entry. Never put a secret in it.

tool.name: logs
tool.title: Read Parallax's logs
tool.description: Read Parallax's logs database: without id, the open entries newest first, one compact row each (filter by status, kind, q, since; limit). With id, that entry with its body and evidence listed; with id and evidence (a path like first/log.txt), that piece's text. Each entry is a failure with its evidence (Parallax's log lines before it, the stack or hang file, a system snapshot, a CPU profile for a slow daemon, what an agent filed). `parallax logs pull <id>` writes an entry and all its evidence to a folder to work from.

tool.name: pr_status
tool.title: Pull request status
tool.description: The cached state of a pull request (your session's when you name none): open/merged/closed, draft, mergeable, and the head's checks. Parallax reads GitHub once for every session through its shared reader; do not poll with `gh api` or `gh pr checks`. wait (seconds, at most 60) holds until state or checks change, then answers the new reading (changed: true); 0 or omitted answers now. stale: true says GitHub's budget is spent or low and this is its answer as of as_of, for the reason in why.

tool.name: window_act
tool.title: Press, type into or toggle a control in the window
tool.description: Work one control of the Parallax window in the background, as a screen reader does: press, focus, set_value (with value), increment, decrement or scroll_into_view the node with id from window_read (a unique name works too). The window may sit behind other apps or hidden; the person's mouse, keyboard and focus are never touched. Answers what it did ("Pressed Settings → Profile"), the screen after it and what changed in the tree; an id that is not on the window is refused with the nearest ones. It presses a merge, stop, send, update or approval only while the person's autonomy lets that kind act on its own (else use the tool for it, which asks them), and never what spends money, places or ends a sign-in or key, or deletes. Each act is in Achilles' ledger, with Undo when it has one.

tool.name: releases
tool.title: Merged pull requests and their release stage
tool.description: Every Parallax Desktop pull request merged to main in the last hours (24 when omitted), read-only, from local git and GitHub's REST API: merged_at; release, the first release whose tag holds its merge commit (absent: not released yet); on_mirror, whether that release is on the public mirror every Mac updates from, and public, the first mirror release that holds it; installed, whether the daemon running here holds it; stage (live, public, released, unreleased, unknown). blocks say in plain words what holds each stage: main does not build (the open "Release blocked" issue), GitHub Actions refused the release or mirror workflow (its budget), the release Mac's fallback still building or uploading, mirror lag, or the app waiting for an idle moment to install. summary leads with how many are not live and how long the oldest has waited; gaps say what could not be read (GitHub's rate limit). It lists the ones not live here, newest first (more counts any left out); all adds the live ones. It answers within about 1.5 s: the first read takes longer, so stale then says to call again. Use it for proof that merged changes reached the installed app, and pr_status for one pull request. It never merges, releases or runs a workflow.

tool.name: pipeline
tool.title: Pipeline metrics
tool.description: The factory's pipeline from a task queued to its change live in the app, stage by stage, over the last hours (24 when omitted, or 48), read-only: queued → placed, placed → agent working (fetch and setup), working → PR opened, local tests (time, fail rate, and failures the environment caused against a failing test), PR opened → checks done, review-bot wait, conflicts and mending, merged → released (with the release Mac's build and publish from its release.log), and released → live (public on the mirror every Mac updates from). Each stage has n (passes that finished in the window), median_s and p90_s in seconds, prev_median_s and trend (slower, faster, steady) against the window before, open (still in it) and oldest_open_s, and unmeasured when no source here measures it. factory_failed counts environment failures (env_failed) and failed mends: factory bugs to repair, never evidence of poor planning. For tests, tested excludes environment failures, test_failed counts actual failing tests, and test_fail_rate is test_failed/tested; no tested runs means quality is unmeasured. fail_rate remains the operational failure rate including environment failures. A failing test alone does not establish a bad plan. bottleneck is the stage that holds work longest now (its median, or its oldest open pass when that is longer, so a release stuck for 40 minutes is named), and summary says it in one line with its trend. Read it to choose what to fix next in the factory: fix the bottleneck first. Sources are session events, the track record, GitHub's REST API through the shared budget (never GraphQL) and the release Mac's ~/.parallax-release/release.log; gaps say what could not be read. It answers within about 1.5 s: the first read takes longer, so stale then says to call again.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Parallax to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Parallax to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://parallax-relay.fly.dev/mcp/NH3P6WthYIHBCyzWj5ZaSg.

_published_faq.name: Is Parallax MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Parallax scores 96/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Parallax's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Parallax scores 90/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 16 of 16 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Parallax?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Parallax in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.
